classification.difficultyReason: Follow the scaffold through two alternate-segment/common-angle similarity proofs, match the ordered side ratios and combine those ratios into the final identity.

content.prompt: In the diagram, $MS$ and $MT$ are tangents from an external point, $M$.

spec.description: Circle with collinear B, A, M; chords BS, SA, BT, TA; tangents MS and MT; and the seven supplied side labels.
spec.mathematics: B and A are exact intersections of y=-0.5 with the unit circle. S and T are exact tangent contacts from M=(2.4,-0.5). BS=a, SA=x, BT=y, TA=b, AM=m, MS=MT=t.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied letters and lengths are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle MSA$ is similar to $\triangle MBS$.

answer.short: $\angle MSA=\angle MBS$ and $\angle SMA=\angle BMS$, so $\triangle MSA\sim\triangle MBS$ (AA).
answer.worked:
$\angle MSA=\angle MBS$ by the alternate segment theorem for tangent $MS$ and chord $SA$, since $B,A,M$ are collinear.

Also, $\angle SMA=\angle BMS$, since $MA$ and $MB$ are the same ray.

Therefore $\triangle MSA\sim\triangle MBS$ (AA), with $M\leftrightarrow M$, $S\leftrightarrow B$ and $A\leftrightarrow S$.

Corresponding sides of the similar triangles in part a give
$$\frac{BS}{SA}=\frac{SM}{AM}.$$
Substituting the diagram labels gives
$$\frac{a}{x}=\frac{t}{m}.$$

$\angle MTA=\angle MBT$ by the alternate segment theorem for tangent $MT$ and chord $TA$.

Also, $\angle TMA=\angle BMT$, since $MA$ and $MB$ are the same ray.

Thus $\triangle MTA\sim\triangle MBT$ (AA). Corresponding sides give
$$\frac{BT}{TA}=\frac{TM}{AM},$$
so
$$\frac{y}{b}=\frac{t}{m}.$$

Parts b and c give
$$\frac{a}{x}=\frac{y}{b}.$$
Multiplying both sides by $bx$ gives
$$ab=xy.$$
